transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-01-17 14:00 UTC
- Duration: 54 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Alex Morales (BrightWave Head of Search), Samira Khan (BrightWave Eng Manager), Devin Park (BrightWave ML Engineer), Rita Gomez (BrightWave Product)

Summary:
Quick hosted API demo focusing on embeddings + reranker endpoints, walkthrough of Redwood Console rerank visualization and Optimize suggestions for batch/caching. Agreed to a 2-week pilot: BrightWave will supply a labeled query set; Redwood will provide sample notebook, pricing, and a pilot SOW.

Topics:
- BrightWave current stack and pain points
- Embeddings quality and dimension choices
- Reranker endpoint behavior and scoring schema
- Console trace and per-route latency/cost breakdowns
- Pilot scope, success criteria, and timeline

Action items (captured during call):
- Jordan to share pilot pricing and draft SOW by 2027-01-20
- Priya to share embedding+rerank sample notebook and console link by 2027-01-18
- BrightWave (Devin) to upload anonymized 10k query examples + labels by 2027-01-22
- Samira to confirm SLA/uptime needs by 2027-01-21

Transcript:
00:00 Jordan Chen: All right everyone can you hear me? Testing, yep. Great, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, I'll run through the hosted API demo and Priya will take the reranker deep-dive.
00:12 Alex Morales: Yep, we can hear you. Thanks Jordan. Quick context from our side, we're BrightWave, we power search across several retail clients, latency has been creeping up with our current vector store setup.
00:23 Jordan Chen: Thanks Alex. Can you give us the stack real quick? Vector store, any on-prem constraints, legal or compliance stuff?
00:31 Samira Khan: Sure, currently using OpenSearch + Pinecone for embeddings, host the front-end on GCP, some customers require EU data residency. We want to avoid heavy infra ops and reduce per-query cost.
00:45 Priya Nair: Cool, that helps. Today we'll demo embeddings endpoint to show similarity vectors and then the reranker endpoint which consumes candidate docs and returns final scores and explanations. We'll also show Optimize suggestions in the Console for batching and caching.
01:00 Jordan Chen: Quick FYI on pricing tiers for hosted: the per-embedding and per-rerank unit pricing—I'll follow up with a detailed sheet after the call.
01:10 Devin Park: One quick question from me before the demo, what's the expected embedding dimensionality? Our embeddings are 768 today, but we've been thinking of switching to 1,024 for better nuance.
01:22 Priya Nair: Short answer: 768 is fine for many retrieval jobs; 1,024 gives more headroom but increases compute and storage. In Redwood Console we show per-model perf curves. For pilot we can try both and report MRR/latency.
01:36 Marcus Li: Also want to note that our hosted reranker is tolerant to different embedding dims—there's transparent vector projection if needed. That often makes the migration smoother.
01:47 Alex Morales: Great. Show us the API calls, pls. We want to compare request/response shape to our current client code.
01:53 Priya Nair: Sure. I'll paste an example request in the chat, but verbally: embeddings endpoint -> POST /v1/embeddings with document text, returns an embedding vector and metadata. Reranker -> POST /v1/rerank with candidate doc list and query embedding or raw query; returns scores and optional explanation tokens.
02:12 Priya Nair: (chat paste) Example body: {"query":"red shoes size 10","candidates":[{"id":"doc_1","text":"..."},{"id":"doc_2","text":"..."}],"top_k":5} Response: {"results":[{"id":"doc_2","score":0.92},{"id":"doc_1","score":0.58}],"explanations":[...]}
02:36 Samira Khan: The explanations bit—are they deterministic? We rely on stability for regression alerts.
02:43 Priya Nair: Good callout. Reranker explanations are post-hoc feature at the moment—deterministic under the same model/version and request shape. We also maintain model versioning and you can pin a version in the Console.
02:58 Jordan Chen: I'll also flag that Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization or smaller model variants when quality delta is acceptable, which cuts cost. But for initial pilot we recommend full precision to measure baseline.
03:14 Rita Gomez: When you say reranker consumes candidates—do we have to run retrieval separately? We run a separate candidate fetch right now with Pinecone.
03:22 Marcus Li: Yes you fetch candidates (we support any vector store) then call rerank; or you can use our retriever + rerank flow in the Console which bundles them. Many customers keep their vector store but call Redwood rerank as a second stage.
03:36 Devin Park: Is there support for batching candidates? We have queries that return 100 candidates, it would be great to score them in one call.
03:44 Priya Nair: Absolutely. Rerank accepts up to N candidates per request—practical limits and latency trade-offs are in Console Optimize. For high throughput, we recommend batching at the retrieval layer into pages of ~32-64 to balance latency/cost.
03:58 Alex Morales: Can you show the Console?
04:02 Priya Nair: Yep switching screens — give me a sec.
04:20 Priya Nair: (screen share) Here's the Redwood Console route page. You can see per-route token/cost and latency histograms. For rerank route I've highlighted a trace — this one shows retrieval latency 24ms, rerank 112ms, total 136ms.
04:45 Samira Khan: That's helpful, what about cost breakdown per token vs per-rerank unit?
04:52 Jordan Chen: In the Console we show cost per route in dollar cents — embeddings, rerank units, and storage. For this trace the rerank dominated cost due to candidate count. Optimize recommended reducing candidate set and using caching on stable queries.
05:10 Devin Park: What's caching look like? Prefix caching?
05:15 Priya Nair: We do prefix and query-key caching for popular queries. Also KV cache for common contexts. If you have stable product pages we can cache candidate vectors and short-circuit rerank for identical queries.
05:28 Alex Morales: Ok demo the reranker scoring differences — maybe show an example where semantic relevance vs lexical disagree.
05:34 Priya Nair: Good call. I'll run a query for "durable hiking boots" against a small sample docs set.
05:40 Priya Nair: (types) Sending request now...
05:50 Priya Nair: Response back — candidate ordering from vector similarity: doc_3, doc_7, doc_1. Reranker scores change order: doc_7 (0.87), doc_3 (0.83), doc_1 (0.41). Explanation suggests doc_7 had stronger product attributes match ("waterproof, 3-year warranty") which boosted final score.
06:10 Alex Morales: Nice, that matches what we want. How do you handle fairness/biased signals? We sometimes have brand boosts baked into our features.
06:18 Marcus Li: You can pass per-candidate metadata or feature weights into rerank. We offer a policy layer in the Console to clamp or adjust scores for specific brands or patterns. We also have audit logs so you can trace why a doc was promoted.
06:34 Samira Khan: Speaking of audit logs, we need SOC2 and the usual security docs — we handle PII, and some EU customers require data residency.
06:44 Jordan Chen: Understood. We'll include SOC2 report, data residency options, and our private deployment docs in the follow-up package. Our hosted API supports region-specific endpoints and you can opt for Private if residency is strict.
06:58 Rita Gomez: For our pilot we probably want hosted but region set to eu-west-1. Is that configurable?
07:04 Jordan Chen: Yes, region selection is part of the route config. We'll note eu-west-1 for the pilot.
07:12 Devin Park: Back to performance — in heavy tails our p95 latency spikes. How do you recommend smoothing that?
07:20 Priya Nair: A few levers: smaller candidate pages for rerank, pre-warming dedicated pools if you need consistent p95, and using the Console autoscaler hints in Optimize to set burst limits. Also automatic fallback to a lighter model variant if p95 crosses SLO.
07:38 Alex Morales: Is fallback automatic or we have to configure rules?
07:42 Marcus Li: You configure fallback policies per route — we provide sensible defaults like fallback to smaller model or region alternate. For pilot we'll help set that up.
07:51 Samira Khan: Show the sample notebook for embedding evaluation?
07:55 Priya Nair: Opening the sample Notebook now — I pushed a Colab that computes MRR, NDCG, and compares dims 768 vs 1024. It also shows how to call the embeddings endpoint in Python.
08:10 Priya Nair: (reads snippet) code: from redwood import Client; c = Client(api_key); emb = c.embeddings.create(texts=[...], model="rw-embed-768"); Then rerank: c.rerank.score(query="...", candidates=[{...}])
08:25 Devin Park: Quick tech: do you return float32 vectors? And are they normalized?
08:30 Priya Nair: We return float32 by default, normalized L2. You can request raw (non-normalized) if you need dot-product semantics.
08:40 Alex Morales: For integration we'd probably use normalized and dot product in our retrieval to keep parity.
08:44 Jordan Chen: Also note we can supply precomputed embeddings upload APIs if you want Redwood to store and serve them — which can reduce per-query compute if the dataset is static.
08:56 Samira Khan: That might be useful for product catalogs. What's retention for precomputed store?
09:02 Jordan Chen: Retention is configurable per account; default is 90 days for hosted, longer for Dedicated. We'll include exact tiers in the follow-up doc.
09:12 Rita Gomez: How do we monitor quality regressions across rollouts?
09:17 Marcus Li: Console has eval suites. You upload a labeled eval set, pin to a route, and any model change that degrades NDCG triggers regression alerts. We can also run canary traffic split for 5-10% to validate.
09:33 Alex Morales: OK great. Any limitations on candidate size or total tokens in rerank request?
09:40 Priya Nair: There are practical limits — token budget per request is around 16k for the hosted reranker right now. We document precise numbers in the API reference; for large candidate sets we recommend chunking.
09:50 Devin Park: For our dataset we might end up chunking. Do you have helper libraries?
09:54 Priya Nair: Yes, our SDK has batching helpers, and the sample Notebook includes a chunk-and-score utility.
10:02 Jordan Chen: Let's talk pilot scope — what would success look like? Alex?
10:06 Alex Morales: Primary goal: improve MRR by >8% on our top queries while keeping p95 under 300ms for EU region. Secondary: reduce per-query cost by 15% within the first month.
10:16 Samira Khan: We also need to validate audit logs and SOC2 compliance for our procurement checklist.
10:22 Jordan Chen: Perfect. We'll capture those as pilot success criteria. I'll send the SOW and pricing; Priya will send the Notebook and Console access. We recommend a 2-week pilot where Redwood runs an A/B test on a subset of traffic.
10:35 Rita Gomez: Any pitfalls customers see during pilots?
10:39 Marcus Li: Common ones: insufficient labeled evals (makes it hard to measure improvement), not isolating feature differences (embedding dim + reranker model change at once), and forgetting region selection. We'll provide a checklist.
10:52 Devin Park: For the reranker model — are you using a transformer cross-encoder? And can we bring our own model?
10:58 Priya Nair: We use a light cross-encoder family tuned for rerank. For Private/Dedicated customers we can support bringing custom models (BYOM) under an enterprise agreement. For hosted we manage the model lifecycle.
11:12 Alex Morales: Good. On competitors — we evaluated Pinecone + an internal reranker but integration complexity was high. How do you differ?
11:20 Jordan Chen: Our differentiation is unified runtime plus Console: observability (trace-level), Optimize suggestions, and transparent model/versioning for production. We'll also help tune candidate size and rerank thresholds for cost.
11:32 Samira Khan: Can we get a timeline for the deliverables?
11:35 Jordan Chen: Sure — deliverables: pricing/SOW by 2027-01-20, Notebook + Console link by 2027-01-18, pilot kickoff week of 2027-01-25. BrightWave supplies labels by 2027-01-22.
11:48 Alex Morales: Sounds good. One last question: does Redwood support differential privacy or KMS encryption for embeddings at rest?
11:56 Marcus Li: We support KMS-backed encryption (customer-managed keys) for Private deployments; for hosted we support our managed KMS and are evaluating differential privacy hooks as an opt-in. We'll include the current security posture in the follow-up package.
12:12 Jordan Chen: Great. We'll wrap up with next steps in the follow-up email. Any final Qs?
12:18 Rita Gomez: No, thanks — looking forward to the sample notebook.
12:22 Devin Park: Same.
12:25 Jordan Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up.
12:29 Alex Morales: Thanks Jordan, Priya, Marcus.
12:33 (call ends)
